Your attack surface is bigger than your application.

Security effort tends to go where the engineering effort goes: into the application. An attacker looks at six layers and uses whichever one gives way first.

  • A phishing email handing over credentials.

  • An injection flaw or broken access control.

  • An endpoint returning another user’s data.

  • A leaked access key or an account without MFA.

  • An exposed admin port or an unpatched laptop.

  • A public storage bucket or an over-permissive IAM role.

One weak layer is enough. See how we cover all six→

Security that goes beyond the report.

A report is where a lot of security work stops. It is roughly where the useful part begins.

We are also a product company. We ship our own security software, which means we know what a fix costs an engineering team, and we write our findings with that in mind.

How we think about security→
Attacker perspective
We start from what someone would actually try, not from a checklist.
Engineering depth
We build software ourselves, so findings arrive with the context an engineer needs.
Outcome first
The goal is a system that is harder to attack, not a longer document.
Practical remediation
Every finding says what to change, and which to change first.
Clear scope
You know what is being tested, what is not, and why, before work starts.
Transparent engagement
No surprises about what we are doing or what we found.
